channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: Critical java-21-openjdk Update for RHEL 10
item.description: Red Hat released a critical security update for java-21-openjdk on RHEL 10, addressing multiple high-severity vulnerabilities. The update, rated as Critical by Red Hat Product Security, contains patches for CVEs that could allow remote code execution with a CVSS score above 8.0. Administrators should apply the update immediately or upgrade to the latest RHEL 10 release to ensure protection.

item.title: Critical java-17-openjdk Update for RHEL 8
item.description: Red Hat issued a critical security update for java-17-openjdk on RHEL 8, fixing several high-severity flaws. The patches address CVEs that could enable remote code execution with CVSS scores exceeding 8.0, posing significant risk. Systems administrators should apply the update promptly or upgrade to the latest RHEL 8 release to mitigate the vulnerabilities.

item.title: Ransomware Brokers Shift Listings to Private Channels
item.description: Ransomware gangs are moving access-broker listings from public dark-web forums to private channels, cutting early warning signals. ZeroFox data shows monthly victim counts rose from 573 in 2025 to 718 in 2026, while public listings dropped from 620 to 370 per quarter. Security teams should monitor private broker communications and employ network segmentation to limit lateral movement once compromised.

item.title: Ukraine, FBI Arrest Ransomware Group Members
item.description: Ukrainian authorities and the FBI arrested four suspects from an international ransomware group tied to more than $40.5 million in ransom payments from at least 28 companies. The raid followed a joint investigation that traced the gang’s stolen-credential phishing attacks. Officials advise organizations to strengthen access controls and monitor for anomalous credential activity to mitigate similar threats.

item.title: Azure Linux 4 Released for VMs Without Extra Fee
item.description: Microsoft announced general availability of Azure Linux 4, its in-house Linux distribution for customer virtual machines and scale sets. It is offered at no extra license fee, with customers paying only for Azure compute. The release enables organizations to deploy a consistent Linux environment across Azure workloads without additional licensing costs.

item.title: Ubuntu Patches Multiple OpenJDK 27 Flaws
item.description: Ubuntu released a security update addressing multiple remote vulnerabilities affecting the OpenJDK 27 environment. Flaws including CVE-2026-114938 and CVE-2026-114939 involve improper input handling and authentication in Compiler, JGSS, and JSSE components, allowing unauthorized data access, denial of service, or arbitrary code execution. Security teams should apply the USN-9158-1 package updates to mitigate potential exploitation.

item.title: USN-9157-1: OpenJDK 25 vulnerabilities
item.description: A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2026-114938) It was discovered that the JGSS component of OpenJDK 25 did not correctly authenticate users. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to read or modify sensitive data. (CVE-2026-114939) Nicholas Carlini discovered that the JSSE component of OpenJDK 25 did not correctly authorize users.

item.title: USN-9156-1: OpenJDK 21 vulnerabilities
item.description: A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2026-114938) It was discovered that the JGSS component of OpenJDK 21 did not correctly authenticate users. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to read or modify sensitive data. (CVE-2026-114939) Nicholas Carlini discovered that the JSSE component of OpenJDK 21 did not correctly authorize users.

item.title: USN-9155-1: OpenJDK 17 vulnerabilities
item.description: A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2026-114938) It was discovered that the JGSS component of OpenJDK 17 did not correctly authenticate users. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to read or modify sensitive data. item.title: USN-9154-1: OpenJDK 11 vulnerabilities
item.description: A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to read or modify sensitive data. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to read or modify sensitive data. (CVE-2026-114940) It was discovered that the Hotspot component of OpenJDK 11 did not correctly authorize users.

item.title: Social Media Amplifies Outage Panic
item.description: The article warns that recent outages and attacks can cause unnecessary worry, especially when amplified by social media. It advises against allowing social media narratives to transform a technical bug into a perceived disaster, which can mislead stakeholders. Readers are encouraged to verify incidents through official sources before reacting, thereby reducing panic and misinformation.

item.title: Chrome for Android Update
item.description: We've just released Chrome 159 (159.0.8154.18) for Android to a small percentage of users. It'll become available on Google Play over the next few days. If you find a new issue, please let us know by filing a bug .

item.title: OpenJDK 17.0.21.1 Critical Update for Portable Linux
item.description: The update addresses multiple vulnerabilities in OpenJDK 17.0.21.1 for portable Linux builds. Red Hat Product Security rates the flaws as critical, with CVSS base scores listed in the CVE references. The vendor has released a patch; administrators should apply the update immediately to mitigate potential exploitation and verify installation promptly.

item.title: SmarterMail Vulnerabilities Affect Builds Before 9817
item.description: SmarterMail versions prior to Build 9817 contain undisclosed vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to compromise the application. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security issued advisory AV26-1177, urging administrators to review links and apply updates as soon as possible. Applying the latest SmarterMail release or patch mitigates the risk; security teams should verify installation and monitor for anomalous activity.

item.title: TeamCity Vulnerabilities in Versions Before 2026.1.3
item.description: TeamCity releases before 2025.11.7 and 2026.1.3 contain vulnerabilities that may enable unauthorized code execution. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security advisory AV26-1176 recommends reviewing links and installing the latest patches immediately. Applying the updated TeamCity version eliminates the flaw; administrators should verify deployment and monitor for suspicious activity and ensure proper configuration.

item.title: Iranian Groups Hand Off Access for Destructive Attacks
item.description: AttackIQ research examined 20 Iranian state-sponsored threat groups, revealing a coordinated hand-off of network access to enable destructive operations. The analysis shows espionage, ransomware, and hacktivism tactics intertwining within state-backed campaigns, complicating attribution and mitigation. Security teams should monitor for lateral movement indicators and implement strict network segmentation to reduce the impact of such hand-offs.

item.title: Admin Plans Early Patch Info Sharing with Industry
item.description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin announced a policy to engage industry for early patch information before releases. The initiative aims to collect detailed patch data from vendors to assess security impact and mitigate potential vulnerabilities. No vendor patch or technical fix is involved; the program is a strategic outreach effort to improve patch management.

item.title: Critical Java and NGINX Vulnerability CVE-2026-114938
item.description: A critical vulnerability disclosed today, identified as CVE-2026-114938, affects Java and NGINX, while a separate Microsoft 365 outage was reported. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution through malformed input, with public proof-of-concept code available, potentially compromising affected servers. Administrators should apply vendor-issued patches for Java and NGINX immediately and monitor Microsoft 365 for service restoration.

item.title: Wellington IT Breach Exposes 50 Credit Unions
item.description: A cyberattack on Wellington IT exposed sensitive member data from 50 credit unions, primarily in Ireland. The breach likely involved credential compromise or unauthorized access to the provider’s systems, though the exact vector remains undisclosed. Affected institutions should conduct forensic investigations, reset credentials, and notify regulators while Wellington IT is advised to strengthen access controls.

item.title: Cisco Endpoint Connector Vulnerabilities Affect Linux, Mac, Windows
item.description: Cisco disclosed vulnerabilities in Secure Endpoint Connector for Linux, Mac, and Windows affecting versions before 1.29.3, 1.27.5, and 8.6.4. The flaws allow local privilege escalation via improper input validation, with public proof-of-concept code available, potentially enabling attackers to gain elevated access. Administrators should upgrade to the latest Secure Endpoint Connector releases and apply vendor-issued patches to mitigate the risk.

item.title: USN-9153-1: cloud-init vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that cloud-init incorrectly handled certain errors when configuring user passwords on systems with SSSD installed but not configured. An attacker could possibly use this issue to access affected user accounts without a password, resulting in unauthorized access.

item.title: F5 NGINX Vulnerabilities CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633
item.description: F5 disclosed vulnerabilities in NGINX Plus and Open Source, CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633, affecting versions before 37.3.0.1, 37.0.8.1, 37.2.0.1, 37.0.7.1, 1.31.9, and 1.30.7. The flaws allow remote code execution via malformed HTTP/2 requests, with public proof-of-concept code available, potentially enabling attackers to compromise servers. Administrators should upgrade to the latest NGINX releases and apply F5-issued patches immediately.

item.title: Chrome Early Stable Desktop Update Released
item.description: Google Chrome released an early stable update for desktop platforms, version 159.0.8154.13/.14, targeting Windows and Mac users. The update includes minor bug fixes and performance improvements, with a full change log available in the release notes. Users are encouraged to install the update via the browser's update mechanism; no security patches are addressed in this release.

item.title: NGINX HTTP/2 Flaw Enables Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
item.description: A decade-old vulnerability in NGINX's HTTP/2 implementation (CVE-2026-123007) allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on servers with HTTP/2 enabled. The flaw, present since version 1.9.5, stems from improper handling of HTTP/2 frames leading to memory corruption and unauthenticated remote code execution. F5 released patched versions 1.31.9 and 1.30.7; administrators must upgrade immediately to mitigate exploitation risk.

item.title: Chrome Beta Desktop Update Released
item.description: Google Chrome updated its Beta channel to version 159.0.8154.13 for Windows, Mac, and Linux desktop users. The release contains incremental bug fixes and stability improvements, with a partial change log posted in the Git log. Users should update via the browser's update settings; no critical security patches are included currently.

item.title: CVE-2026-130638 - Path traversal in the object detection dataset preparation tool in AutoGluon MultiModal
item.description: Bulletin ID: 2026-188-AWS Publication Date: 11/18/2026 10:00 AM PST Description: Relative path traversal in the object detection dataset preparation tool in AutoGluon Multimodal before 1.6.0 might allow adversary-in-the-middle attackers to write arbitrary files with the privileges of the user running the tool via a crafted dataset archive substituted for a dataset downloaded over plaintext HTTP.

item.title: GhostMap eBPF Rootkit Conceals IronWorm Malware on Linux
item.description: Attackers are deploying the GhostMap eBPF rootkit to hide IronWorm malware processes, files, and network sockets from standard Linux inspection tools like /proc/net/tcp. The rootkit leverages extended Berkeley Packet Filter hooks to manipulate kernel-level visibility, allowing malicious listeners to evade detection while remaining operational.

item.title: Arctic Wolf Releases Quarterly Innovation Update
item.description: Arctic Wolf published its November 2026 quarterly update, outlining new product features, strategic initiatives, and upcoming roadmap milestones. The release highlights enhancements in threat detection, managed detection and response services, and expanded partner integrations. Customers are encouraged to review the full briefing for detailed feature specifications and to schedule a roadmap discussion with Arctic Wolf.

item.title: Hackers Use Hidden Cron Jobs to Reinstall Malware on Firewalls and Routers Every 5 Minutes
item.description: A Linux botnet is hiding in a place most network teams never look: the scheduled jobs on their firewalls, routers and switches. If a responder kills the malware and deletes the file, a hidden cron job downloads it again within five minutes.

item.title: Critical Apache Roller RCE Flaw Under Active Exploitation, No Authentication Required
item.description: A critical security flaw in Apache Roller, an open-source, Java-based blogging platform, has come under active exploitation in the wild, according to the Apache Software Foundation (ASF) The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS score: 9.8), is a case of unauthenticated deserialization in the XML-RPC endpoint that could lead to remote code execution.

item.title: OffSec Converts Recent Vulnerabilities Into Hands-On Labs
item.description: OffSec released over 80 hands-on labs built around recent real-world vulnerabilities including PHPH2Shell, expanding its training catalog within two weeks. The labs map to actual CVEs and support a Level 20 Learn One promotion offering $550 off for enrolled learners. Security teams can use the curriculum to practice detection and remediation techniques against these threats.

item.title: RHSA-2026:100573: Critical: OpenJDK 25.0.5.1 Security Update for Portable Linux Builds
item.description: An update is now available for OpenJDK. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Critical. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: NGINX HTTP/2 Flaws Enable Remote Code Execution
item.description: Two critical NGINX HTTP/2 vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007) enable remote code execution on servers accepting HTTP/2 connections. The flaws trigger memory corruption during HTTP/2 stream handling; CVSS scores 9.8 and 9.6, and no public exploit yet but potential for server compromise. NGINX released patches on November 18, 2026; administrators should update to the latest release or disable HTTP/2 until patched.

item.title: Cisco Patches ClamAV Flaws Causing Denial of Service
item.description: Cisco addressed multiple ClamAV vulnerabilities affecting its products that let a remote attacker bypass configured file and scan time limits, causing denial of service that interrupts scanning operations. The Security Impact Rating is High on Windows platforms like Cisco Secure Endpoint Connector, Medium elsewhere, with no available workarounds. Cisco released software updates; administrators should apply them promptly.

item.title: Vulnerability in Oracle OpenJDK (Java4Shell) Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
item.description: On November 17, 2026, Oracle announced the availability of fixes for a vulnerability in OpenJDK that could lead to remote code execution identified by CVE-2026-114938. For additional information, see the Talos blog post: Talos Threat Advisory CVE-2026-114938: Critical vulnerability in OpenJDK JAVA This advisory will be updated as additional information becomes available.

item.title: Emacs Prior to 31.2 Allows Local Code Execution
item.description: GNU Emacs versions before 31.2 contain a local code execution flaw triggered by malicious .dir-locals.el files. The vulnerability bypasses auto-mode-alist checks, allowing an attacker to run arbitrary code when a user opens a file; no public exploit reported. Users should upgrade to Emacs 31.2 or later, or disable .dir-locals.el processing until a patch is released.

item.title: Armornet Launches AI-Driven Supply-Chain Risk Platform
item.description: Armornet introduces an AI-driven platform that maps teams’ vendor dependencies and assigns continuous risk scores to each supplier. The solution monitors the software supply chain from code to deployment, providing real-time visibility into potential security gaps. Security teams can use the platform’s insights to prioritize remediation and enforce stricter vendor controls.

item.title: Russian State Hackers Exploit Stolen Cloud Data for Espionage
item.description: Russian state-backed threat actors leverage stolen cloud credentials to impersonate legitimate contacts and infiltrate target organizations. The method bypasses authentication, granting attackers access to internal networks and enabling data exfiltration from professional contacts; no specific vulnerability exploitation is reported. Security teams should enforce multi-factor authentication, monitor for anomalous login patterns, and review cloud access logs for suspicious activity.

item.title: From Deepfakes to Helpdesk Impersonation: Why Stronger Verification Matters
item.description: Attackers are using deepfakes, helpdesk impersonation, and fake IT support requests to deceive employees and gain unauthorized access to corporate systems. Specops Software examines real-world attacks and explains how stronger identity verification can help organizations prevent social engineering threats.

item.title: Cloudflare WAF Blocks Java4Shell Exploit
item.description: Java4Shell, a critical memory-corruption flaw in OpenJDK’s Base64 decoder, allows remote code execution on affected Java runtimes. Identified as CVE-2026-114938, the vulnerability exploits a decoder buffer overflow triggered by crafted Base64 payloads, enabling unauthenticated code execution. Cloudflare’s WAF now offers six managed rules that log matching requests by default; organizations should also apply the latest OpenJDK patches.

item.title: British Hacker Sentenced Six Years for Crypto Theft
item.description: Tyler Robert Buchanan, a 24-year-old from Dundee, received a six-year prison sentence for orchestrating an $11.6 million cryptocurrency theft operation. Microsoft labeled the group as one of the most dangerous financial criminal collectives, targeting victims via phishing and credential theft. Law enforcement agencies should continue monitoring for related phishing campaigns and enforce stricter credential hygiene to mitigate similar attacks.

item.title: OX Security Unveils OX Radar and Response Center
item.description: OX Security launched OX Radar and Response Center, a platform that automatically monitors critical vulnerabilities and supply chain threats for customers. The system aggregates threat data, evaluates exposure, and prioritizes remediation, enabling teams to focus on high-priority risks. No vendor patch is required; organizations should integrate the tool into existing workflows for continuous threat visibility.

item.title: New EggStreme Malware Variant Goes Silent to Evade Security Tools in Government Attacks
item.description: The suspected Chinese advanced persistent threat (APT) group behind the sophisticated EggStreme malware has rebuilt its toolkit as it continues to target government organizations in the Philippines. "When attackers are exposed, the cheap response is to rotate," Bitdefender said in a technical report shared with The Hacker News.

item.title: Microsoft’s AI Uncovers 99 Security Issues in Express, ImageMagick and Other Open-Source Projects
item.description: Microsoft and GitHub sent 99 verified security reports to six open-source projects, including Express and ImageMagick, after an AI pilot identified thousands of potential vulnerabilities. In its Nov. 17 announcement, GitHub said maintainers had fixed 55 issues as of Nov. 15.

item.title: Brazilian Signature Apps Harbor RCE Vulnerabilities
item.description: Brazilian government-sanctioned signature apps expose authentication middleware to remote code execution via unvalidated input. The flaw lets attackers inject code during document signing, potentially compromising legal documents and enabling fraud; no public exploit confirmed. Patches are pending; security teams should disable vulnerable middleware, apply vendor updates when released, and monitor for unauthorized signing activity.

item.title: GitHub security advisory (AV26-1172)
item.description: Serial number: AV26-1172 Date: November 18, 2026 As of November 18, 2026, GitHub is affected by vulnerabilities in the following product: Enterprise Server 3.19.0 Prior to 3.19.16 3.20.0 Prior to 3.20.12 3.21.0 Prior to 3.21.10 3.22.0 Prior to 3.22.5 The Cyber Centre encourages users and administrators to review the provided web links and apply any necessary updates as they become available.

item.title: Gentlemen Ransomware Gang Claims NVIDIA Breach
item.description: The Gentlemen ransomware group posted a claim of breaching NVIDIA on its dark-web leak site. The post includes a countdown and ransom talk references but lacks sample files or confirmed compromise evidence. NVIDIA has not publicly confirmed a breach, and no definitive proof of infiltration has been disclosed in the public domain.

item.title: Russian APT Impersonates Hacked Firm Employee to Target US Org
item.description: A Russian APT used stolen Star Blizzard credentials to pose as an employee of a compromised firm and phish a U.S. organization. The attack leveraged data and social engineering to gain initial access by exploiting the target's trust in the impersonated identity. Security teams should verify employee identities, enforce MFA, and monitor for anomalous credential usage to mitigate impersonation attacks.

item.title: Malwarebytes Engineers Secure Their Own Antivirus
item.description: Malwarebytes engineers discuss protecting their antivirus platform from malware that could disable or bypass its defenses. The article outlines defensive strategies, including code integrity checks, runtime monitoring, and secure update mechanisms to thwart disabling attacks. Security teams should adopt similar integrity verification and update safeguards to maintain antivirus resilience against disabling malware.

item.title: Google Chrome Vulnerability Affects Versions Before 158.0.8127.36
item.description: A vulnerability affects Google Chrome stable channel desktop versions before 158.0.8127.36 on Windows, Mac, and Linux. The flaw, lacking a CVE ID, is not publicly exploited but could enable code execution or session compromise. Google advises users to review the advisory and install the latest Chrome update promptly to mitigate the risk.
